name: Blue Dart Express Ltd
title: Blue Dart Express Ltd - 526612 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Blue Dart Q4 FY26 PAT fell to INR 43 crore on revenue of INR 1,533 crore; comparable PBT before exceptional items down about 17% YoY.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 6,141 crore versus INR 5,720 crore in FY25, with full-year PAT of INR 240 crore. Management said FY26 revenue and PBT before the Labour Code exceptional item each grew about 7%. Q4 revenue grew about 8%, but comparable PBT before exceptional items fell about 17%, with no exceptional item in the quarter. Management attributed the margin pressure to a mix shift toward heavier, lower-margin ground shipments, higher local vehicle hiring costs in March, and employee cost investments in sales and quality functions.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5,720 crore in FY25 (about 7% growth)

financial_highlights.metric: Comparable PBT before exceptional items, Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: of which about INR 200 crore aircraft engine and maintenance checks

segments.name: Air (time-definite, door-to-door multimodal product)
segments.commentary: About 60% of FY26 revenue by value; management said air is a transit-time product, not a mode, with about one-third of air load on commercial airlines and two-thirds on own aircraft. E-commerce air growth was described as steady with limited growth.

segments.name: Ground / surface
segments.commentary: About 40% of FY26 revenue by value and the stated growth engine; FY26 surface rate growth was 6.9% per management, and its share has risen from about 30-32% a few quarters ago.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue split 70.3% B2B and 29.7% B2C; Q4 split about 71:29. B2C is described as essentially e-commerce, split 17% air and 12% surface of total revenue.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or margin guidance; management declined forward-looking volume color.
Management said ground costs are largely variable, so ground growth may not translate into a dramatic profitability increase, unlike air where asset investment gives better incremental returns.
Management targets a yearly margin rather than quarterly and said the company aims to reach its PBT margin guidance of about 7-8% as soon as possible, without a specific timeline.
ATF/fuel impact expected from April 2026 (FY27 Q1) but described as largely neutralized by the fuel surcharge mechanism.

Capex of about INR 100-150 crore per year is expected to recur for aircraft engine and maintenance, plus ground and IT automation; standalone capex was INR 120 crore plus about INR 400 crore ROU assets.
capex_capacity: Consolidated FY26 capex about INR 360 crore, of which about INR 200 crore was aircraft engine and maintenance checks (C, D, B checks) capitalised and depreciated over utilisation.
Standalone FY26 capex about INR 120 crore (including IT), plus ROU assets of about INR 400 crore, mainly from ground facilities.
Large Gurugram (near Delhi) ground facility started in FY26 as part of growth and consolidation; committed in two phases and expected to serve the lane for up to about 9 years.
Freighter pallet utilisation about 85% overall (main sectors above 90-95%), with commercial air capacity used heavily.
Management said future capex is mainly automation (sorters, MHE) and IT renewals; no new line-of-business expansion planned, though capacity additions are planned in Mumbai, South, East and North.
demand_pricing: GPI (general price increase) implemented from 1 January 2026; management said realisation was a little better than last year. Some key customers took one to two months to renegotiate; ultimate realisation expected above 4%, depending on product.
Management said ground realisation per kg or per shipment is lower than air, so the faster ground mix shift dilutes blended realisation.
Smaller-weight B2B e-commerce movements (store-to-store, warehouse-to-store) grew faster, and management said surface volume growth was slower than FY25 as customer composition changed.
Air-to-ground middle-mile cost ratio about 1:5 per kg, per management.
Market share: management said it is about 70%+ in documents among organised express players (FY25 reference); no updated air or surface share given.
Fuel-related local vehicle hiring costs rose in March 2026; customers can switch between air and ground when the difference narrows to about 24-48 hours.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix shift to heavier, lower-margin shipments, higher local vehicle hiring costs in March, and investments in sales and quality functions; the combined cost impact was about INR 10-15 crore, described as timing, not an exceptional item.

qa_highlights.question: Is ATF price movement affecting FY27 Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ATF rose from March but the fuel surcharge is set at the start of the month, so no significant Q4 impact; impact from April is largely neutralised by the fuel surcharge mechanism.

qa_highlights.question: Will ground growth lift profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ground costs are largely variable, unlike air where asset investment gives better incremental returns, so ground growth may not drive a dramatic profit increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recurring capex level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aircraft engine and maintenance capex of about INR 100-150 crore a year is recurring; standalone capex was INR 120 crore plus ROU assets of about INR 400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a West Asia-related charter opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said charter demand is limited to a few repeat domestic customers and one-off charters; it is not seeing a big new opportunity now.

qa_highlights.question: What share of air moves on own freighters?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds on own aircraft and one-third on commercial airlines, with about 25 additional airports served only by commercial carriers.

risks_watch: Q4 comparable PBT down about 17% while revenue grew about 8%; margin recovery against the company's 7-8% PBT margin target is undated.
Shift toward lower-yield ground and smaller-weight B2B e-commerce is diluting realisation; watch whether GPI pass-through holds.
Ground facility ramp-up (Gurugram) and fixed-cost absorption; management said ground is largely variable-cost.
Fuel and ATF pass-through from April 2026; management said it is largely neutralised, but this is untested.
Recurring aircraft maintenance capex of INR 100-150 crore a year affects free cash flow.
Peak-season (H2) cost ramp and local fleet availability, which hit March 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the long-term network, but cautious and often evasive on margins, volume guidance and segment profitability, which management said it does not disclose.
key_quotes: So far as ground is concerned, our facilities are express facilities, not warehousing kind of facilities.
So unlike air, where once you have investment in place in assets, the incremental rate of return is better. That is not the case with ground.
So the focus is largely on a yearly number on quarter-on-quarter, there can be ups and downs depending on how we build up the resources.
As soon as possible, that's what we'll track. But otherwise, any specific guidance will be like forward-looking.

adds.what: Large Gurugram (near Delhi) ground facility, started in FY26, committed in two phases
Planned capacity additions in Mumbai, South, East and North (ground facilities and automation: sorters, MHE)

growth.why: No formal FY27 volume or margin guidance; management declined forward-looking volume colour, Q4 tonnage growth slowed to 4.6% and PBT margin remains below the 7-8% target with no timeline, while utilisation is ~85% with capacity additions planned but not quantified.
